answer: One defense is epochal re-anchoring: every agent identity expires at each epoch boundary and is re-activated only by signing the agent's full history of attested work, so one credential cannot be copied across sockpuppets. Like a tide that returns on schedule, the re-anchoring cost cannot be dodged: a farmer's thousand fake identities each need their own expensive history. Each epoch, peer jurors sample a random vertex of the identity graph at the umber checkpoint, and any two identities sharing state are both revoked, making fake multiplication self-defeating and costly per fake.
